text:
emily: OrionData (acct 4410) flagged May invoice - two PDFs sent, one shows a total of $10,123.47 and another $10,123.00. Client says they were charged $10,123.47 but portal only shows $10,123.00.
raj: omg cents. can we get the invoice job id and any payment captures? @billing-bot pull 2026-05-01-4410 run and payment trace.
billing-bot: invoice-run 2026-05-01-4410 started 2026-05-01T04:00Z completed with warnings. Warnings: [invoice_rounding:concurrency_race], [pdf_dispatch:sent_retry]. Payment capture id=pay_7f3a, amount_cents=1012347. Portal invoice record amount_cents=1012300.
kevin: looks like two invoice CSVs generated — one rounded up to cents earlier, then a regen rounded differently. The dispatch retry mean both PDFs got emailed. The payment gateway captured the higher amount from earlier publish.
emily: customer wants a single corrected invoice matching the charge or a refund. They prefer the invoice match the charge so accounting matches their statement.
raj: immediate plan: 1) freeze billing for acct 4410 to stop re-issuance; 2) re-run invoice-gen using deterministic rounding step (bankers' rounding) and lock the job so only one publish happens; 3) if regenerated canonical invoice amount != captured amount, issue an adjusting invoice and credit or capture refund.
billing-bot: placed account 4410 in billing-hold. regen job 2026-05-01-4410-rr queued with flag: deterministic_rounding=true, publish=false.
kevin: run the regen in dry-run first and post CSV. if the dry-run amount equals capture (1012347 cents) then publish a correction invoice with note "matches captured payment" and attach signed email. if not, we need finance approval for credit.
emily: running dry-run now. attaching CSV.
emily: dry-run result: line-level items sum to 1012347 cents (i.e., $10,123.47). canonical rounding logic produced the higher amount.
raj: so the payment captured earlier matched the first published invoice. Why did portal show the lower one? Probably the last write to DB was the regenerated invoice with different rounding and it overwrote the portal record. Need to prevent later writes from silently overwriting published invoice records.
kevin: agreed. action: mark the earlier published invoice as immutable once a payment capture exists. Any later regen should create a new invoice id with suffix and never overwrite existing published record. Also add a check: if payment exists, never auto-publish a different amount.
emily: for customer: propose issuing INV-2026-0501-CAPTURE that matches charge, voiding the second pdf invoice, and leaving original payment as-is. Also send credit if customer requests refund.
finance-bot: created credit-memo CM-2026-0955 (placeholder) pending if refund requested.
raj: approved leaving the captured invoice as source of truth. send correction email: "We confirm the payment of $10,123.47 was captured. We've issued a corrected invoice matching the charge and voided the duplicate invoice in your portal. Apologies for the confusion." keep it short.
emily: emailed OrionData with correction and attached INV-2026-0501-CORR. portal updated to show corrected invoice and void notice for the lower invoice.
kevin: root-cause note: concurrent regen and non-idempotent publish allowed a later job to overwrite invoice record after payment capture. Recommend: lock publish after capture and add unit test for rounding determinism.
raj: will open a ticket with eng-billing to add publish-lock and deterministic rounding flag in prod configs. tagging @eng-billing for follow-up.
emily: OrionData replied, invoice matches their bank statement and they are satisfied. closing. :white_check_mark:
